sources.title: C. E. Bosworth: Saffarids, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct scholarly article read, political history and cultural patronage. Distinguishes Laythid first line and Khalafid second line. Overview, mapped-century periods, literature and end counted together; no nationalism or first-Persian-poet claim adopted.

sources.title: C. E. Bosworth: Yaqub ibn Layth, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct scholarly article read. Coppersmith origin, accession 861, capture of Nishapur 873, defeat in Iraq, campaigns with captives and booty. Page has obvious converted-date typographical errors (257/970, 258/972), not used. The 876 defeat is cross-supported by the main Saffarid article.

sources.title: C. E. Bosworth: Amr ibn Layth, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct scholarly article read. Caliphal appointment and tribute; defeat near Balkh in 900, subsequent contraction. Does not adopt the article’s wrong caliph name for Amr’s 902 execution or impose a precise 879-901 regnal endpoint on the 900 capture.

sources.title: C. E. Bosworth: Divan, government office, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct Saffarid administration paragraph read: military register and pay allotments in government building at Zarang, Amr’s three treasuries. No inference that modern ministry structures existed.

sources.title: Guy Le Strange: The Lands of the Eastern Caliphate (1905), p.337
sources.note: British Library volume W15/8578 hosted by Qatar Digital Library; direct digitized text read. Printed p.337 summarizes tenth-century Istakhri/Ibn Hawqal/Muqaddasi: canals, two reservoirs, outer-town houses and sardab cellars, wind/sand, mosque choked by sand in the 970s. Later fourteenth-century gardens and legendary dyke founders not attributed to Saffarids.

sources.title: Michael Harverson: Mills in Iran, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct Windmills section read: Masudi’s tenth-century statement of mills grinding grain and raising water in Sistan. Separates contemporary evidence from his much earlier anecdote about Umar. No claim that surviving seventeenth-century mills are Saffarid buildings.

sources.title: Sadeq Sajjadi: Bimarestan, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct page partially extracted; targeted original indexed query with Amr and bazar exposes the complete relevant paragraph, independently corroborated by Czarnuszewicz 2025, Medical manuscripts and history. Amr’s market income funded Zarang hospital and congregational mosque; founding date of hospital uncertain.

sources.title: Marc Czarnuszewicz: New insights into Sistani intellectual culture under the Saffarids (2025)
sources.note: Full open-access original research article read through publisher redirect, Journal of Islamic Studies 36(2), pp.266-288. The Kunnash and Medical manuscripts and history sections: Abu Sahl al-Sijzi, dedication to Khalaf, later Istanbul copies, royal medicine attributions and transmission limits. Manuscript copy dates do not date original composition.

sources.title: Helmand Sistan Project: Shahr-i Gholghola, Citadel Palace
sources.note: Original excavators’ entire page and image captions read via indexed text; direct web extraction shows headings only. Exact targeted site query returns full palace description. Three storeys, 55 by 55 m, circulation, inferred functions, 1974 trench and dated pottery; Saffarid attribution based on architecture and ceramics. Do not claim building function of inaccessible first floor as proven.

sources.title: Helmand Sistan Project: Shahr-i Gholghola
sources.note: Original excavators’ full indexed page read. Gazetteer 1006, Nimroz/Sar-o-Tar, not the famous similarly named Bamiyan site. Mosque, bazaar, caravanserai and eastern elaborate homes; later bathhouse explicitly Ghaznavid. Identification as medieval Taq is probable, not certain.

sources.title: Ashmolean Museum, Heberden Coin Room: Saffarid dirham HCR14180
sources.note: Direct detail-page access failed; exact query HCR14180 returned full original catalogue. Dynasty Saffarids, Khalaf ibn Ahmad, Sijistan mint, silver dirham, AH 390 / AD 1000, Arabic transcription and English translation; SICA 7:418. Modern purchase in 1966, no excavation context asserted. Unlike misleading collection-list snippets, individual record identity checked.

proposedOverrides.name: Saffarids
proposedOverrides.summary: Sistan-based dynasty whose ninth-century empire became a smaller regional realm.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact indexed ID, no existing runtime card/override or staged collision. Imported world-900 polygon spans 50.53-71.02 E and 23.68-37.52 N, extending far beyond the tenth-century Sistan realm. Public opening explicitly warns that the broad polygon cannot represent the full 900-1000 period. Earlier imperial phases are labelled, and the 1003 conquest lies after coverage. First Laythid line, second Khalafid line, subsequent dynastic claims distinguished; no Safavid confusion and no extra IDs attached. Shahr-i Gholghola is HSP site 1006 in Nimroz/Sar-o-Tar, not Bamiyan’s similarly named site. Preserve atlas bounds, no silent geometry repair.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Coin HCR14180 is actually Saffarid Khalaf, unlike nearby Banijurid catalogue entries that appeared in broad search results. Original catalogue AH 390 / AD 1000 matches end of coverage; authentic Arabic mint formula, not an invented Persian vernacular specimen.
